answer.rationale: Memory b1 confirms a release rollback previously cleared a checkout error spike cleanly with no customer impact, establishing rollback as a proven recovery path on this stack. Memory b5 confirms that routing read traffic off the primary recovers write latency the same day, which is relevant context but not the lever I am pulling now. The write path is the bottleneck at peak settlement, latency is already 5x target and rising, and a release went out 2 hours ago — this is the strongest correlative signal and b1 shows the prior build was stable. Rolling back the release is the single intervention most likely to restore write latency without dropping writes, matching the primary objective of sustained availability. I am not confident the rollback alone will fully resolve the degradation — settlement peak load may persist — so I am flagging downstream value risk and keeping read-replica routing and capacity add as queued follow-ons for the next intervention window.
